A graded relationship between GDMT intensity and survival was observed. Center-level variability was negligible (intraclass correlation coefficient 0.02).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In patients with CS supported by Impella, early GDMT implementation was feasible in a substantial proportion of patients. Greater GDMT exposure at device explantation was associated with lower in-hospital mortality. Ventricular unloading may provide an opportunity to initiate outcome-modifying therapies during the acute phase of CS.

articles.conclusion: In patients with CS supported by Impella, early GDMT implementation was feasible in a substantial proportion of patients. Greater GDMT exposure at device explantation was associated with lower in-hospital mortality. Ventricular unloading may provide an opportunity to initiate outcome-modifying therapies during the acute phase of CS.

articles.title: Ventricular Assist Devices Effectively Bridge Pediatric Patients to Heart Retransplantation: An ACTION Registry Study
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)

abstract.text: The use of ventricular assist devices (VAD) in pediatric patients as a bridge to heart transplantation has increased over the past two decades. However, the use of VAD to bridge pediatric transplant recipients to retransplantation is rare and under-studied. We performed a retrospective study using the Advanced Cardiac Therapies Improving Outcomes Network (ACTION) registry to evaluate patient characteristics and clinical outcomes in patients bridged to retransplant with VAD. A total of 24 patients were identified and supported for a median duration of 64 days (interquartile range [IQR]: 15.0-101.25). Of these, 54% (n = 13) were implanted as a bridge to retransplant candidacy (BTC) and 46% (n = 11) as a bridge to retransplant (BTT). We found a high prevalence of major adverse events, including infection in 75% (n = 18), bleeding in 42% (n = 10), renal dysfunction requiring dialysis in 33% (n = 8), and stroke in 8% (n = 2). Despite this, 71% (n = 17) survived to retransplant, with an 88% 1 year survival following retransplant. Device mortality was higher in BTC compared to BTT (46% vs. 9%; p = 0.046). Our study is the first multicenter study evaluating the use of VAD as a BTT. We exhibit a high prevalence of adverse events on VAD, but a favorable waitlist and post-retransplant survival.

articles.title: Initial Experience with Bachmann Bundle Pacing Lead Implantation as a Rhythm Control Strategy in Atrial Fibrillation
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND AIMS
abstract.text: Bachmann bundle pacing (BBP) is challenging during atrial fibrillation (AF) because ECG based endpoints cannot confirm lead positioning. We aimed to demonstrate the feasibility of a practical approach to BBP implantation during AF and propose a framework for comprehensive conduction system pacing with BBP and left bundle branch pacing (LBBP) for rhythm control in patients referred for pace-and-ablate therapy.

abstract.label: METHODS AND RESULTS
abstract.text: Twenty-four consecutive patients with persistent or longstanding persistent AF and preserved ejection fraction underwent dual-chamber BBP and LBBP implantation with individually optimized pacing rate and AV interval. Twelve underwent BBP during AF (Group 1) and 12 during sinus (Group 2), including six cardioverted intraprocedurally. During AF, lead positioning was guided by anatomical landmarks, local electrograms, current of injury, and impedance changes. After sinus rhythm restoration, BBP was confirmed in 11/12 Group 1 patients. Reductions in P-wave duration and interatrial block were observed in both groups. Seventeen had been referred for pace-and-ablate therapy; three in Group 1 reverted spontaneously to sinus rhythm before cardioversion. Over a median 192 [139-212] days after sinus restoration, 12/17 maintained sinus rhythm; 2 underwent AV node ablation, 1 AF ablation, 1 repeat cardioversion, and 1 required rate-control medication for paroxysmal AF. No complications occurred.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: BBP implantation during AF is feasible using anatomical and electrophysiological markers, with Bachmann bundle capture confirmed after sinus rhythm restoration. Exploratory findings suggest that comprehensive conduction system pacing with BBP and LBBP may support a rhythm-control (pace-and-wait) strategy in persistent AF patients referred for pace-and-ablate therapy.

articles.conclusion: BBP implantation during AF is feasible using anatomical and electrophysiological markers, with Bachmann bundle capture confirmed after sinus rhythm restoration. Exploratory findings suggest that comprehensive conduction system pacing with BBP and LBBP may support a rhythm-control (pace-and-wait) strategy in persistent AF patients referred for pace-and-ablate therapy.

articles.title: Chronic Organizing Mediastinal Hematoma Causing Mechanical Prosthetic Tricuspid Valve Dysfunction

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Mechanical prosthetic valvular dysfunction is typically thought to be secondary to thrombosis or pannus formation on the valve. Cross-sectional imaging can help with identification of the etiology of prosthetic valvular dysfunction.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 39-year-old man with tricuspid atresia and prior biventricular repair with a right atrial to right ventricular conduit presented for an increasing mechanical tricuspid valve gradient and change in his valve clicking sound. Fluoroscopy revealed reduced disc excursion. Three doses of low-dose thrombolytics were trialed without improvement. Computed tomography imaging suggested an intermediate-density mass compressing the conduit and causing extrinsic dysfunction of the tricuspid prosthesis. Surgical examination revealed a chronic mediastinal hematoma causing conduit compression in addition to pannus formation.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Mediastinal hematomas are rare and typically provoked by trauma but can be spontaneous particularly with warfarin anticoagulation.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGE
abstract.text: Mechanical tricuspid prosthesis dysfunction is often from thrombosis or pannus formation, but extrinsic compression should additionally be considered.

articles.title: Longitudinal Changes in Left Atrial Stiffness Index Improve Risk Stratification in Patients with Hypertension
articles.journal: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography : official publication of the American Society of Echocardiography

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Left atrial (LA) stiffness index is a non-invasive echocardiographic parameter reflecting left ventricular filling pressure; however, its prognostic significance in hypertension remains unclear. We aimed to assess the prognostic value of the longitudinal change in LA stiffness index in patients with hypertension.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We analyzed 1,442 hypertensive patients from the STRATS-HHD registry who underwent echocardiography including LA and left ventricular (LV) strain at baseline and 6-18 months. Patients were categorized into four groups according to longitudinal changes in LA stiffness index: Low-Low, High-Low, Low-High, and High-High, using a data-driven prognostic cut-off of 0.63 (Low <0.63; High ≥0.63). The primary outcome was a composite of hospitalization for heart failure (HHF) and cardiovascular death, and secondary outcomes included HHF and incident atrial fibrillation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 1,442 patients, 996 (69.1%) were classified as Low-Low, 173 (12.0%) as High-Low, 91 (6.3%) as Low-High, and 182 (12.6%) as High-High. Over 5 years, Low-High (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 2.175, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.048-4.515, P=0.037) and High-High (aHR 2.935, 95% CI 1.697-5.076, P<0.001) groups were associated with a higher risk of the primary outcome, whereas the High-Low group showed a similar risk to the Low-Low group. Similar trends were observed for HHF and incident atrial fibrillation. Beyond clinical factors and LV mass index, LA stiffness index provided greater incremental prognostic value than individual echocardiographic markers, including LASr and E/e'.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: LA stiffness index was associated with clinical outcomes in hypertension, and longitudinal changes provided additional prognostic information. Trajectory assessment may refine risk stratification.

articles.conclusion: LA stiffness index was associated with clinical outcomes in hypertension, and longitudinal changes provided additional prognostic information. Trajectory assessment may refine risk stratification.

articles.title: Preoperative Six-Minute Walk Distance Predicts Mortality After Durable Left Ventricular Assist Device Implantation
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)

abstract.text: Accurate preoperative risk stratification remains a challenge in advanced heart failure before durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation. We assessed whether preoperative six-minute walk distance (6MWD) was associated with all-cause mortality and compared its discrimination with peak oxygen uptake (pVO2). In this retrospective single-center cohort (January 2016-May 2025), 136 of 206 implanted patients had an eligible preoperative 6MWD. Deaths through May 29, 2026, were ascertained from recorded death dates. During follow-up, 85 patients died; median observed follow-up was 871.5 days. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.712 for 6MWD (n = 136) and 0.639 for pVO2 (n = 127); paired comparison in 127 patients showed no significant difference (DeLong p = 0.212). Each 50 m increase in 6MWD was associated with lower mortality (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.88, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.79-0.98). Patients walking less than 350 m had worse survival (log-rank p = 0.002; HR: 1.98, 95% CI: 1.27-3.11). The association persisted after adjustment for age, INTERMACS profile, and device type (HR: 2.12, 95% CI: 1.27-3.54). Preoperative 6MWD may contribute to risk stratification before durable LVAD implantation; the threshold requires external validation.

articles.title: Sex differences in mechanical circulatory support efficacy in infarct-related cardiogenic shock. An individual patient data meta-analysis
articles.journal: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care
articles.journal_abbrev: Eur Heart J Acute Cardiovasc Care
articles.ta: Eur Heart J Acute Cardiovasc Care

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Routine use of active mechanical circulatory support (MCS) in infarct-related cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) remains controversial. Although recent evidence suggests potential benefit in selected patients, the influence of sex on MCS efficacy is poorly defined.

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: To evaluate whether sex modifies the effect of MCS in AMI-CS.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Randomized trials comparing early routine MCS with standard care in AMI-CS and reporting 6-month mortality were identified through January 2025. Individual patient data were analyzed using study-stratified Cox models. The primary outcome was 6-month all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included 30-day mortality, major bleeding, and peripheral ischemic vascular complications.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Nine trials including 213 (20%) female and 845 male patients were analysed. Women were older than men (67.6 vs. 63.7 years; P < 0.001) and had higher 6-month mortality (60% vs. 52%; P = 0.03). Early routine MCS was not associated with significantly lower mortality in either women (HR, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.70-1.42) or men (HR, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.70-1.02; P for interaction = 0.41). Among DanGer Shock-like patients, MCS was associated with lower mortality in men (HR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.51-0.86), but not in women (HR, 1.18; 95% CI, 0.72-1.91; P for interaction = 0.02). MCS increased complications in both sexes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Women with AMI-CS were underrepresented and had higher mortality than men. No sex-specific treatment effect was observed overall, whereas subgroup findings suggested possible heterogeneity in DanGer-Shock-like patients. These findings, limited by small number of female patients and wide confidence intervals, support the need for adequately powered trials with sufficient female representation.

articles.conclusion: Women with AMI-CS were underrepresented and had higher mortality than men. No sex-specific treatment effect was observed overall, whereas subgroup findings suggested possible heterogeneity in DanGer-Shock-like patients. These findings, limited by small number of female patients and wide confidence intervals, support the need for adequately powered trials with sufficient female representation.

articles.title: Deep Learning-Based Classification of Pulmonary Hypertension Using Early-Fused CTPA and Pulmonary Artery Segmentation Maps

abstract.text: Computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) is vital for diagnosing pulmonary hypertension (PH), especially thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH). However, manual image interpretation of CTPA often leads to misdiagnosis. This study aims to automatically segment the pulmonary artery from CTPA images and develop a deep learning model by fusing CTPA images with pulmonary artery segmentation results to distinguish pulmonary hypertension (PH vs. subjects without PH (no-PH)) and its PH subtype, CTEPH (CTEPH, other PH vs. no-PH). The study included 92 patients with CTEPH, 85 patients with other types of PH, and 140 no-PH. We completed the image preprocessing and segmentation of the pulmonary arterial tree of all the sample data. Based on four deep learning model classifiers-ResNet50, DenseNet, SENet, and Swin Transformer, we respectively developed four distinct network architectures: Single input channel for CTPA images, as well as early, middle, and late fusion strategies that combine CTPA images with their corresponding pulmonary vascular segmentation maps. The performance of the testing experiments has shown that the DenseNet (CTPA-seg) early fusion model achieves optimal performance in the binary classification task of pulmonary hypertension (PH vs. no-PH), with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.927. Meanwhile, the Swin Transformer (CTPA-seg) early fusion model shows the best performance in the ternary classification of pulmonary hypertension subtypes (CTEPH, other PH vs. no-PH), achieving an AUC of 0.855. Compared with models that only use clinical images, the early feature fusion strategy shows significantly higher accuracy in classifying and diagnosing PH, which is beneficial for the differential diagnosis of CTEPH.

articles.title: SysteMatic LeARning With Technology in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension (SMART PAH): A Mixed Methods Pilot Feasibility Study of the Impact of Video-Assisted Education in PAH

abstract.text: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) carries physical, emotional, and psychosocial burdens. Despite therapeutic advances, patients report limited disease understanding. The Systematic Learning with Technology in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension (SMART PAH) study evaluated feasibility and utility of a video-assisted education intervention. We conducted a mixed-methods pilot study in PAH. Participants accessed 12 web-based videos and completed pre- and post-intervention assessments over 4 weeks. Outcomes included PAH knowledge, Patient Activation (PAM), Patient Health Questionnaire-8 (PHQ-8), Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7), and EmPHasis-10 scores. Usability was assessed using the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool and semi-structured interviews. Descriptive statistics and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests were used. Eighteen patients were enrolled (median age 59 years; 67% female; 44% idiopathic PAH, 27% connective tissue disease (CTD)-associated PAH). Most were WHO Functional Class II (50%), and 71% were low-risk by REVEAL Lite 2, with a median 6-min walk distance of 425 m. Post-intervention, PAM scores significantly improved (p = 0.014), indicating patient activation. Secondary outcomes showed trends toward improvement (PHQ-8: 4.0 → 2.5, p = 0.23; GAD-7: 2.5 → 1.0, p = 0.72; EmPHasis-10: 15 → 9, p = 0.18). Knowledge gains were greatest for "Travel & Living with PAH" (p = 0.18) and "Palliative Care & PAH" (p = 0.026). Qualitative analysis identified domains through which the intervention supported patient needs. Participants described the program as accessible, empowering, and confidence-building. SMART PAH was feasible, acceptable, and associated with improved patient activation. Limited by sample size, findings suggest that video-based education may address informational gaps and enhance patient engagement in PAH. Further studies are needed to evaluate long-term effects on patient-centered and clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Epigenetic DNA Methylation Patterns Stratify Heart Failure Phenotypes and Predict Clinical Outcome

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Environmental and lifestyle exposures contribute substantially to heart failure (HF) development and progression. DNA methylation integrates cumulative environmental exposures and may provide insight into biological pathways and risk stratification across HF phenotypes.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: The aim of this study was to identify phenotype-specific DNA methylation patterns across HF subtypes and evaluate their association with clinical outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Individuals with symptomatic HF (universal definition stage C or D; HF with preserved ejection fraction, HF with mildly reduced ejection fraction, and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction [HFrEF]) from the MyoVasc (An Epidemiological Cohort Study to Investigate the Development and Progression of Heart Failure and the Interaction With Vascular Disease) cohort (N = 3,289) and individuals without cardiovascular disease from the population-based GHS (Gutenberg Health Study) (N = 18,700) were analyzed. Genome-wide DNA methylation from whole blood was measured using the Illumina Infinium MethylationEPIC array. Phenotype-specific DNA methylation scores were derived using penalized regression models adjusted for cardiovascular risk factors.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Distinct and partially overlapping DNA methylation patterns were identified across HF phenotypes, with limited overlap at the CpG level but substantial convergence at the gene level. Phenotype-specific methylation scores discriminated patients with HF from control subjects with high accuracy (area under the curve: 0.97-0.98). Methylation signatures in HF with preserved ejection fraction were associated predominantly with metabolic and inflammatory markers, whereas HFrEF signatures were more strongly linked to markers of myocardial injury and vascular disease. All methylation scores were independently associated with composite of cardiac death or hospitalization for worsening HF and all-cause mortality, with the strongest association observed for the HFrEF score (HR: ∼1.7 per SD).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Symptomatic HF phenotypes are characterized by distinct and shared DNA methylation signatures. These epigenetic profiles reflect relevant biological pathways and are associated with adverse clinical outcomes, supporting their potential utility in HF risk stratification and precision medicine.

articles.conclusion: Symptomatic HF phenotypes are characterized by distinct and shared DNA methylation signatures. These epigenetic profiles reflect relevant biological pathways and are associated with adverse clinical outcomes, supporting their potential utility in HF risk stratification and precision medicine.

articles.title: Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement in an Incomplete Ring With LAMPOON Facilitated By Aortic Prosthesis

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Transcatheter mitral valve replacement in large incomplete flexible mitral bands is high risk because limited anchoring and anterior leaflet displacement may cause embolization or left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 54-year-old man with ischemic cardiomyopathy, prior coronary artery bypass grafting, aortic valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement, mitral repair with a 31-mm Duran AnCore band, and tricuspid annuloplasty presented with NYHA functional class IV heart failure from severe recurrent mitral regurgitation. Computed tomography excluded SAPIEN M3 (predicted neo-LVOT 0 mm2) and showed a long anterior mitral leaflet, raising concern for dynamic obstruction despite a predicted neo-LVOT of 347.6 mm2 for a 29-mm balloon-expandable valve. He underwent antegrade base-to-tip laceration of the anterior mitral leaflet to prevent outflow obstruction, followed by valve-in-ring transcatheter mitral valve replacement, with no paravalvular leak or significant LVOT gradient.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Anterior aortic prosthetic anatomy facilitated valve anchoring despite the incomplete flexible band, which would have been prohibitive in the absence of anterior bioprosthesis.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGE
abstract.text: Adjacent prosthetic anatomy may be leveraged in selected complex valve-in-ring procedures after meticulous multimodality planning and procedural expertise.

articles.title: Prognostication of end-stage heart failure using a machine learning model based on haemodynamics and cardiac energetics data

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: In the evolving landscape of heart failure treatment, clinicians face challenges in predicting which end-stage heart failure patients will require heart replacement therapies, such as left ventricular assist devices or transplantation, or are at risk of death. Traditional risk models often fail to accurately stratify patients due to complex interactions of guideline-directed medical therapy, individual responses, and haemodynamic or shock phenotypes.

abstract.label: METHODS AND RESULTS
abstract.text: This study introduces a novel approach using machine learning to predict patient outcomes by analysing a comprehensive set of haemodynamic variables, including metrics tied to cardiac energetics-an emerging field focused on heart energy dynamics during failure. A dataset of 2904 patients across the spectrum of heart failure was used to train and test the models, which underwent rigorous model selection, cross-validation, and hyperparameter tuning on 70% of the data, using forward feature selection. Metrics for the remaining 30% used for testing resulted in an area under the curve of 0.81, a Matthews correlation coefficient of 0.35, and an accuracy of 0.74 to predict the composite endpoint of survival free from death, left ventricular assist devices, or transplant at 1 year. We also demonstrate consistency across the different patient databases used for training, validation, and testing, supported by an F1 score of 0.65 overall and 0.82 for patients who received medical management. The model shows a promising negative predictive value of 0.92, but external validation with a prospective database is needed before clinical application.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This approach is novel in integrating haemodynamics and cardiac energetics with machine learning towards more individualized and effective treatment for heart failure patients.

articles.conclusion: This approach is novel in integrating haemodynamics and cardiac energetics with machine learning towards more individualized and effective treatment for heart failure patients.

articles.title: Anemia and Iron Deficiency Across Renal Function in Hospitalized Heart Failure: Insights From OPPORTUNITIES Registry

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Anemia and iron deficiency (ID) are highly prevalent among patients hospitalized for heart failure (HHF). Their prognostic contributions in the acute setting, particularly across kidney function, remain incompletely understood.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: We investigated the association of anemia, transferrin saturation (TSAT), and ID according to kidney function, with postdischarge outcomes in HHF patients.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Consecutive HHF patients enrolled in the OPPORTUNITIES registry with available hemoglobin and TSAT at discharge. The primary endpoint was HF-free survival, a composite of all-cause death, urgent heart transplantation, heart failure (HF) hospitalization, and urgent emergency department referral for HF worsening at 12 months. Adjusted Cox regression models were applied.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 454 HHF patients were included. The median age was 77 (69-83); 37.9% were women, and 55% of patients were anemic. Anemic patients were older and exhibited a greater burden of comorbidities. Hemoglobin and TSAT showed a modest positive correlation overall (rho = 0.276, P < 0.001), which disappeared in patients with estimated glomerular filtration rate <30 mL/min/1.73 m2. Lower hemoglobin was independently associated with a higher risk (adjusted HR: 0.82; 95% CI: 0.75-0.91; P < 0.001), whereas TSAT was not independently predictive. A significant interaction between hemoglobin and renal function was observed (P = 0.025), indicating that the hemoglobin effect varied according to kidney function. Among ID definitions, only TSAT <20% independently identified patients at an increased risk (HR: 1.44; 95% CI: 1.03-2.03; P = 0.035).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In HHF patients, the prognostic relevance of anemia varies according to renal function. TSAT <20% was the only ID definition independently associated with adverse outcomes.

articles.conclusion: In HHF patients, the prognostic relevance of anemia varies according to renal function. TSAT <20% was the only ID definition independently associated with adverse outcomes.

articles.title: Left Ventricular Unloading With Self-Expanding Pump During Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Acute Myocardial Infarction
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)

abstract.text: Increased left ventricular (LV) afterload and distension during venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) support may impede myocardial perfusion in acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Active LV unloading has been associated with improved outcomes. We report the first clinical use of a self-expanding percutaneous ventricular assist device (NyokAssist; magAssist, Suzhou, China) for LV unloading during VA-ECMO in a 56 year old man with AMI-related cardiogenic shock (CS). Successful coronary angiography and percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) of the culprit left circumflex (LCx) lesion were performed with NyokAssist + VA-ECMO support. The patient was successfully weaned from VA-ECMO on post-procedure day 5 and remained on NyokAssist support alone for an additional 7 days before being transferred on VA-ECMO to a heart transplant center for consideration of advanced heart failure therapies due to limited myocardial recovery. No device-related complications were observed. This case demonstrates the technical feasibility of early implementation of a combined VA-ECMO and NyokAssist support strategy, enabling LV unloading, temporary hemodynamic stabilization, end-organ improvement, and VA-ECMO decannulation in a patient with AMI-related CS. As this report describes a single-patient experience, further clinical studies are warranted to define the safety, efficacy, and potential role of the use of NyokAssist in combination with VA-ECMO in the management of AMI-related CS.

articles.title: Plantain Extract Inhibits PASMC Proliferation and Improves Pulmonary Artery Remodeling in HPH Rats

abstract.text: Hypoxia-induced hyperproliferation of pulmonary smooth muscle cells (PASMCs) and pulmonary remodeling are important features of hypoxic pulmonary hypertension (HPH). This study employed network pharmacology methods and discovered that the crude extract of plantain (PW) exhibits anti-inflammatory and antioxidant stress effects, capable of reducing pulmonary artery pressure and improving pulmonary artery remodeling in COPD rats with HPH. Additionally, the study found that the AU component in PW possesses strong anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities. In this study, PW reduced pulmonary artery pressure and improved pulmonary artery remodeling in rats with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and HPH through its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects. Further research found that aucubin (AU) in PW extract had the strongest antioxidant effects. In the subsequent in vitro experiments, AU enhanced mitochondrial membrane potential in PASMCs exposed to hypoxia, alleviated oxidative stress, and inhibited the excessive proliferation and migration of PASMCs. In vivo experiments demonstrated that AU could alleviate oxidative stress, decrease right ventricular hypertrophy and pulmonary artery pressure, increase Bax expression, reduce Bcl-2 expression, inhibit PASMC proliferation, and improve pulmonary artery remodeling in rats with HPH. In summary, AU from PW extract inhibited hypoxia-induced PASMC hyperproliferation, improved HPH pulmonary remodeling, and reduced pulmonary artery pressure.

articles.title: Left Bundle Branch Optimized Resynchronization Therapy for Persistent Ventricular Dysfunction After Complex PCI and TAVR

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Severe aortic stenosis with complex coronary artery disease presents challenges in patients unsuitable for surgery. Persistent left bundle branch block (LBBB) after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) may impair ventricular recovery.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 67-year-old man underwent high-risk left main-left anterior descending percutaneous coronary intervention, complicated by cardiogenic shock and severe left ventricular (LV) dysfunction. Subsequent TAVR achieved favorable valve hemodynamics but was followed by new-onset left bundle branch block and persistent LV dysfunction. Left bundle branch pacing achieved complete correction only at high output. A coronary sinus lead was added for left bundle branch-optimized cardiac resynchronization therapy with a defibrillator (LOT-CRTD). At 3 months, LV function fully recovered with reverse remodeling and marked symptom improvement. Why Beyond the Guideline: Optimal percutaneous coronary intervention-TAVR timing and device strategies for post-TAVR LBBB with LV dysfunction remain poorly defined in current guidelines.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: LOT-CRTD may provide effective cardiac resynchronization when isolated left bundle branch pacing cannot achieve optimal correction.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGE
abstract.text: Sequence of PCI-TAVR remained individualized. LOT-CRT is a viable strategy to facilitate ventricular recovery for post-TAVR LBBB.

articles.title: Racial and Ethnic Disparities in Postarrest Cardiac Procedures for Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Effective postarrest care facilitates optimal outcomes for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Relatively little research has evaluated whether there may be racial or ethnic disparities in the workup and management of the patient post arrest.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively studied out-of-hospital cardiac arrests using the TriNetX research database. We defined out-of-hospital cardiac arrest as any emergency department visit (2013-2024) with a diagnosis of cardiac arrest and included patients who survived to admission. Multivariate adjusted logistic regression was used to compare rates of the following cardiac interventions across race or ethnicity: (1) echocardiography; (2) left heart catheterization; (3) percutaneous coronary intervention; (4) ventricular assist device placement; and (5) automated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator placement.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 58 394 cases of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest met inclusion criteria. Compared with White patients (left heart catheterization: 13.9%, percutaneous coronary intervention: 7.1%, ventricular assist device: 3.0%, automated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator: 0.9%), Black patients had lower odds of receiving left heart catheterization (7.2%, adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.60 [95% CI, 0.55-0.64]), percutaneous coronary intervention (2.6%, aOR, 0.47 [95% CI, 0.42-0.53]), ventricular assist device placement (1.6%, aOR, 0.70 [95% CI, 0.60-0.80]), and automated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator placement (0.4%, aOR, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.41-0.70]). Hispanic/Latino patients were also less likely to receive left heart catheterization (8.9%, aOR, 0.72 [95% CI, 0.64-0.80]), percutaneous coronary intervention (3.7%, aOR, 0.63 [95% CI, 0.53-0.74]), and automated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator placement (0.4%, aOR, 0.52 [95% CI, 0.33-0.81]).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Our large multicenter analysis identifies racial or ethnic disparities in postarrest cardiac workup and management. Further research is needed to identify potential causes for these disparities with the hope of developing strategies to address them.

articles.conclusion: Our large multicenter analysis identifies racial or ethnic disparities in postarrest cardiac workup and management. Further research is needed to identify potential causes for these disparities with the hope of developing strategies to address them.

articles.title: Sex Differences in Clinical Presentation and Outcomes in Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension: A Japanese Registry

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Sex-related differences in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) remain incompletely defined.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: The authors aimed to evaluate sex differences in clinical presentation, treatment response, and outcomes in a nationwide Japanese CTEPH registry.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We analyzed 1,527 participants in the prospective, multicenter Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension Anticoagulant Registry (UMIN000033784). Baseline and follow-up clinical status, hemodynamics, treatments, morbidity and mortality, and bleeding were compared by sex in the overall and treatment-naïve cohorts using time-to-event and adjusted regression analyses.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Median follow-up was 27.4 months (Q1-Q3: 10.6-49.7) in the overall cohort and 18.6 months (Q1-Q3: 6.4-36.7) in the treatment-naïve cohort. Female patients comprised 1,080 of 1,527 (70.7%) participants and were older, with lower body mass index and shorter 6-minute walk distance than male patients (all P < 0.001). In the overall cohort, pulmonary vascular resistance index was similar between sexes, whereas cardiac index was modestly higher in female patients. Treatment-naïve female patients had worse World Health Organization functional class (P = 0.03) and higher pulmonary vascular resistance index (989.2 ± 480.3 vs 870.6 ± 501.4 dyn s cm-5 m-2; P = 0.04). Crude improvements in exercise capacity and hemodynamics were comparable or greater in female patients but were attenuated after baseline adjustment. Morbidity, mortality, and bleeding did not differ by sex in either cohort.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Female patients with CTEPH, particularly when treatment-naïve, presented with more advanced disease but had comparable long-term outcomes under contemporary multimodal management. These observational associations do not establish treatment efficacy but support sex-specific awareness at diagnosis.

articles.conclusion: Female patients with CTEPH, particularly when treatment-naïve, presented with more advanced disease but had comparable long-term outcomes under contemporary multimodal management. These observational associations do not establish treatment efficacy but support sex-specific awareness at diagnosis.

articles.title: Ultraprocessed Food Consumption and Incident Heart Failure: The Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Ultraprocessed foods (UPFs) are associated with adverse cardiometabolic outcomes and increased atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk. However, the relationship between UPF intake and incident heart failure (HF) remains incompletely understood.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: The aims of this study were to examine the relationship between UPF consumption and incident HF and to evaluate potential biological mediators.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A sample of 6,531 U.S. adults 45-84 years of age without cardiovascular disease at baseline from MESA (Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis) was analyzed. UPF intake was classified according to the Nova system. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models evaluated associations between UPF intake and incident HF. Phenotypes were classified as heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) (ejection fraction <50%) and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) (ejection fraction ≥50%). Mediation analyses were conducted to evaluate the potential mediating role of waist-to-height ratio as a surrogate measure for central adiposity.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Higher UPF intake was significantly associated with increased risk of incident HF across sequentially adjusted models. In the primary model (model 2), each additional daily serving of UPF was associated with a 5% higher risk of incident HF (HR: 1.052; 95% CI: 1.002-1.103). When stratified by phenotype, UPF intake remained significantly associated with HFpEF (HR: 1.096; 95% CI: 1.016-1.183) but not HFrEF. Participants in the upper 80% of UPF intake had a >2-fold higher risk for HFpEF than those in the lowest 20% (HR: 2.234; 95% CI: 1.289-3.874). In mediation analyses, waist-to-height ratio statistically accounted for ∼51% of the association between UPF intake and total HF and 49% of the association between UPF intake and HFpEF.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Higher UPF consumption was significantly associated with an increased risk for incident HF, with associations driven primarily by the HFpEF phenotype. Central adiposity, measured by waist-to-height ratio, demonstrated a potential mediating role, suggesting that obesity-related cardiometabolic pathways may represent an important pathway linking UPF consumption to HF risk.

articles.conclusion: Higher UPF consumption was significantly associated with an increased risk for incident HF, with associations driven primarily by the HFpEF phenotype. Central adiposity, measured by waist-to-height ratio, demonstrated a potential mediating role, suggesting that obesity-related cardiometabolic pathways may represent an important pathway linking UPF consumption to HF risk.

articles.title: Outcomes of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement for Aortic Regurgitation in LVAD Patients: The JENA-VAD Study
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Aortic regurgitation (AR) during left ventricular assist device (LVAD) support causes recurrent heart failure. Surgery is high risk and stenosis-designed valves anchor poorly in noncalcified anatomy.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: The goal of this study was to evaluate early outcomes of the AR-specific Trilogy transcatheter heart valve for LVAD-associated AR.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: JENA-VAD is a prospective, multicenter, single-arm investigational device exemption study. An independent committee adjudicated endpoints using VARC-3 (Valve Academic Research Consortium-3) definitions. The primary efficacy endpoint was the VARC-3 device success composite adapted for LVAD support, and the primary safety endpoint was the VARC-3 early safety composite.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Fifty patients were treated (mean age 69.2 years; 40% female). Median follow-up was 105 days (range 27 to 577 days). Technical and device success were 96.0% (95% CI: 86.3-99.5). Freedom from any component event of the VARC-3 early safety composite was 90.0% (95% CI: 78.2-96.7). At 30 days, 7 VARC-3 safety events occurred in 5 patients: type 2 to 4 bleeding (n = 2), major vascular complications (n = 2), device-related peripheral interventions (n = 2), and new pacemaker (1 of 7 without prior pacing; 14.3%). There were no strokes or myocardial infarctions. Two transient ischemic attacks occurred in patients without valve abnormalities. Beyond 30 days, cardiovascular death occurred in 1 patient (day 86). Follow-up computed tomography (CT) imaging or transesophageal echocardiography was obtained in 12 patients, and 11 (including 3 within 30 days) had leaflet thickening or thrombosis, including all patients who underwent CT. The remaining 38 patients did not have postprocedure imaging. Two of these events were symptomatic: valve thrombosis and a transient ischemic attack (day 116), and prosthetic AR that required valve-in-valve implantation (day 146) and subsequent heart transplantation. In exploratory analyses, NYHA functional class at 30 days was I or II in 72.3% (34 of 47) and Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire overall summary score rose 11.5 ± 21.5 points (n = 44).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Transcatheter valve replacement using a dedicated system in LVAD patients was feasible with high technical and device success and without early death, stroke, or moderate or severe residual AR. Leaflet thickening or thrombosis, detected on clinically indicated CT imaging, occurred in 22%, representing a lower bound. Follow-up is ongoing to inform longer-term safety and effectiveness. (Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement Using the JenaValve Trilogy Heart Valve System for Clinically Significant Aortic Regurgitation in Patients With Left Ventricular Assist Devices [LVAD]; NCT06594705).

articles.conclusion: Transcatheter valve replacement using a dedicated system in LVAD patients was feasible with high technical and device success and without early death, stroke, or moderate or severe residual AR. Leaflet thickening or thrombosis, detected on clinically indicated CT imaging, occurred in 22%, representing a lower bound. Follow-up is ongoing to inform longer-term safety and effectiveness. articles.title: Anti-Kv1.4 antibody-associated myocarditis refractory to maintenance immunosuppressive therapy: a case report

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Anti-Kv1.4 antibody-associated myocarditis is an extremely rare condition and its optimal long-term management remains unclear.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 66-year-old woman presented with myasthenia gravis-like symptoms, marked creatine kinase elevation, leukopenia, and hypogammaglobulinaemia. She developed acute myocarditis with ventricular arrhythmias and a reduced left ventricular ejection fraction. Intravenous immunoglobulin and corticosteroid therapy resulted in rapid clinical and cardiac improvement. During cautious tapering of oral prednisolone, she was readmitted with febrile neutropenia and subsequently developed progressive ventricular dysfunction and cardiogenic shock. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated extensive myocardial fibrosis, and autopsy revealed diffuse lymphocytic infiltration. Post-mortem testing confirmed positivity for anti-Kv1.4 antibodies.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: This case highlights the potentially fatal course of suspected anti-Kv1.4 antibody-associated inflammatory myocardial disease despite an initial favourable response to immunosuppressive therapy. It illustrates the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges of distinguishing immune-mediated progression from other causes of myocardial injury and implies the need for individualized long-term management strategies.

articles.title: Psychiatric comorbidity and disparities in the invasive management of acute myocardial infarction: a national analysis, 2016-23

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: Mental health disorders (MHDs) are common in acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and have been associated with less intensive cardiac care. We examined trends in five MHDs and their adjusted associations with in-hospital mortality, mechanical circulatory support (MCS), and coronary revascularization.

abstract.label: METHODS AND RESULTS
abstract.text: We analysed the National Inpatient Sample, 2016-23, including adult hospitalizations with a principal diagnosis of AMI [ICD-10-CM I21.x/I22.x, excluding type 2 myocardial infarction (MI)]; five MHDs were identified from secondary diagnoses. Survey-weighted logistic regression produced adjusted odds ratios (aORs), adjusting for demographics, hospital characteristics, MI type, and 19 comorbidities, with all five MHDs entered simultaneously. Sensitivity analyses were restricted to hospitalizations without prior MI, percutaneous coronary intervention, or coronary artery bypass grafting. Among 970 969 AMI hospitalizations, prevalence rose for every MHD except schizophrenia/psychotic disorders, most steeply for PTSD (Post-traumatic stress disorder). Schizophrenia/psychotic disorders had the lowest adjusted odds of revascularization [aOR, 0.56; 95% confidence interval, 0.53-0.60] and invasive management (0.52; 0.49-0.55), followed by bipolar disorder (revascularization 0.81; 0.78-0.85); MCS associations were attenuated after adjustment. Restricted to those without prior coronary disease, the schizophrenia deficit was larger (0.54; 0.50-0.57) than among those with prior coronary disease (0.67; 0.60-0.74; interaction P < 0.001). Depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder, and PTSD were associated with lower adjusted in-hospital mortality (all P < 0.001); schizophrenia/psychotic disorders showed no significant difference (1.11; 0.98-1.26; P = 0.09).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Schizophrenia and other psychotic disorders were consistently associated with markedly lower odds of invasive evaluation and coronary revascularization after AMI, with the largest deficit at first presentation. These findings highlight a potentially modifiable gap in cardiovascular care.

articles.conclusion: Schizophrenia and other psychotic disorders were consistently associated with markedly lower odds of invasive evaluation and coronary revascularization after AMI, with the largest deficit at first presentation. These findings highlight a potentially modifiable gap in cardiovascular care.
